source: NCERT Class XII, India — People and Economy, Ch. 7 (Mineral and Energy Resources).

sections.heading: 1. Minerals — Types and Distribution
points: **Minerals** = naturally occurring substances; **metallic (ferrous/non-ferrous), non-metallic, and energy** minerals.
Most minerals are concentrated in the **peninsular plateau** (the north-eastern plateau: Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal).
**Iron ore** — magnetite/hematite (Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Goa).

sections.heading: 2. Metallic and Non-Metallic Minerals
points: **Manganese** (Odisha, MP), **copper** (Rajasthan-Khetri, MP-Balaghat, Jharkhand-Singhbhum), **bauxite** (Odisha, ore of aluminium).
**Mica** — Jharkhand, Andhra, Rajasthan (Koderma = finest).
**Limestone** — for cement/iron smelting.

sections.heading: 3. Energy Resources — Conventional
points: **Coal** — the chief conventional source; **Gondwana coalfields** (Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro), Tertiary coal in NE.
**Petroleum ('black gold')** — Mumbai High, Gujarat, Assam (Digboi); **natural gas**.
**Hydroelectric power** — from dams/rivers.
**Nuclear power** — uses uranium/thorium (Tarapur, Kaiga, Kudankulam etc.).

sections.heading: 4. Non-Conventional Energy and Conservation
points: **Renewables:** solar (huge potential), wind (Tamil Nadu, Gujarat), tidal (Gulf of Kachchh), geothermal, biogas.
**Energy conservation** — efficient use, renewables, reducing waste.
Minerals are exhaustible → need **judicious use and recycling**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Minerals concentrated in the peninsular (NE) plateau: Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh.
Copper = Khetri (Rajasthan); bauxite = ore of aluminium (Odisha).
Gondwana coal: Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro; petroleum = Mumbai High, Digboi.
Wind power = Tamil Nadu, Gujarat; tidal = Gulf of Kachchh.
Minerals are exhaustible → conserve and recycle.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Most Indian minerals are in the **peninsular (north-eastern) plateau**.
**Copper = Khetri (Rajasthan)**; **bauxite = ore of aluminium**.
**Gondwana coalfields** (Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro) hold most Indian coal.
**Digboi (Assam)** was an early oilfield; petroleum = 'black gold'.
